one_liner: RISC-V assembly Keccak, Kyber and Dilithium for RV32/RV64 with B and V; 2-5x fewer cycles than pq-crystals reference C.
what_it_does: Research artifact of the TCHES 2025 paper by Zhang, Yan, Huang and Koç: Keccak-f1600 permutations, Kyber/Dilithium NTTs and polynomial arithmetic written in RISC-V assembly for each ISA combination (RV32IM, RV32IMB, RV64IM, RV64IMB, plus RVV 1.0 variants), wrapped in the pq-crystals C code so the public API is the usual NIST crypto_kem_* / crypto_sign_* calls. Each ISA variant is a separate build selected by Makefile (-march and -DKYBER_K or Dilithium mode); there is no library build, no runtime CPU dispatch and no install target.
how_it_is_fast: Keccak uses lane complementing, a one-round in-place state layout and instruction scheduling for the C908's dual-issue in-order pipeline (CPI about 0.51-0.52 vs 0.57-0.64 for compiled C); RV32IB adds bit interleaving and RV32 with V adds hybrid scalar/vector multi-way Keccak (3-5 states). NTTs use Plantard (scalar) or Montgomery (RVV) reductions with merged layers and no extra modular reduction, plus cached base multiplication; rej_uniform, cbd2/cbd3 and rej_eta are vectorized with vrgather index tables built for VLEN=128.
when_to_use: Kyber/ML-KEM or Dilithium on an in-order dual-issue RISC-V core such as XuanTie C908 (CanMV-K230) or SpacemiT X60, where the paper shows Kyber768 KeyGen 742k to 278k cycles on RV64IM and 165k with B+V.
SHA-3/SHAKE on RV32I or RV64I without the B extension: the scalar Keccak-f1600 is 1.9x (RV64I, 4926 to 2591 cycles) and 2.0x (RV32I, 15779 to 7808) faster than PQClean's fips202.c.
As a source of RISC-V kernels to port into a maintained library; leancrypto already pulled its RV64 ML-KEM/Keccak code (issues #1 and #2).
Studying how to schedule crypto kernels for dual-issue in-order RISC-V cores; the cpi/ directory holds measured instruction latencies for the C908.
when_not_to_use: ML-DSA: the Dilithium code (checked in main's Dilithium/RV64: CRHBYTES 64, no context string) is round-3 Dilithium, not FIPS 204 ML-DSA, so its signatures do not interoperate with ML-DSA; only the main branch's Kyber was updated toward FIPS 203.
RVV on cores whose VLEN is not 128 (or 256 on main for the Kyber NTT): index tables and coefficient layouts are hard-coded for VLEN=128, and the ches2025 branch has no runtime VLEN detection.

Fast Keccak via vectors on RV64: on C908 the pure RVV Keccak costs 4827 cycles per state against 1770 for the scalar RV64IB assembly, and the RV64 hybrid variants never beat scalar (best about 1980 per state), so the Kyber/Dilithium RV64 V builds keep scalar Keccak.

Production use without a side-channel review: the scalar C wrappers keep the pre-KyberSlash division by KYBER_Q in poly_tomsg and poly_compress (see gotchas), and there is no ct-verification tooling in the repo.
Out-of-order or wider RISC-V cores: the scheduling targets dual-issue in-order pipelines and gains elsewhere are not measured.

integration.dependencies: none beyond a RISC-V cross toolchain; measured with the Xuantie-900 GCC 10.4.0 toolchain V2.8.0; main also has Makefile_x60 files for the SpacemiT board
integration.min_toolchain: GCC with RVV 1.0 and Zba/Zbb assembler support (paper used Xuantie GCC 10.4.0; leancrypto's port built it with a distro toolchain using -march=rv64imadcv per issue #2)
integration.platforms: RISC-V only: RV32IM{B}{V} and RV64IM{B}{V}; V variants need RVV 1.0 with VLEN=128 (main adds VLEN=256 Kyber NTT for SpacemiT X60)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the KEM and signature entry points keep the pq-crystals NIST API and test vectors match the reference (make run_diff_vectors), but you must pick per-ISA source sets from the Makefiles and Dilithium is round 3, not ML-DSA

gotchas: KyberSlash pattern still present: Kyber/RV64, RV32 and ref poly.c on both ches2025 and main compute t = (((t << 1) + KYBER_Q/2)/KYBER_Q) & 1 in poly_tomsg (decapsulation, secret-dependent) and divide by KYBER_Q in poly_compress, while upstream pq-crystals/kyber ref/poly.c now uses multiply-and-shift (t *= 80635; t >>= 28). GCC at -O3 usually lowers a constant division to a multiply, so the measured numbers are likely unaffected, but -Os or other compilers can emit a variable-time div; the paper's statement that it avoids secret-dependent timing does not cover these C paths.

Headline ratios mix ISAs: the 4.5x KeyGen figure compares the RV64IMBV build against reference C built for plain RV64IM. The harness also builds the reference with -march=rv64imacv_zba_zbb (Kyber/ref/results_rv64imbv.txt): same-ISA Kyber768 ratios are 3.7x KeyGen (615,950 to 164,706), 4.2x Encaps and 4.9x Decaps; compiler-only V actually slows the reference about 5% (RV64IMV ref KeyGen 779,568 vs RV64IM 742,535).

Two branches: numbers reproduce only from ches2025, whose Makefiles hard-code the board at 192.168.123.99 (root, /sharefs), build with -static and scp/ssh the binaries; main has refactored RVV NTTs, X60 support and FIPS 203 changes and no matching result files for the paper.

Issue #1 (stack smash in polyvec_basemul_acc_montgomery) was a missing ret in leancrypto's copy, not in PQRV; both PQRV branches end every function in ntt_dualissue_plant_rv64im.S with ret. Issue #2 showed the RVV Keccak gives no gain on SpacemiT X60 either (author's 4-way figures: RVV 2415, RV64IM 2580, RV64IMB 1819 cycles).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PQRV when the target is RISC-V; neon-ntt (Armv8 Neon) and pqm4 (Cortex-M4) cover the same Kyber/Dilithium kernels on ARM, and pqm4 is maintained and already tracks ML-KEM/ML-DSA, so prefer it, or leancrypto's RISC-V port, wherever a FIPS-aligned maintained library matters more than raw cycles.
verified_claims_summary: On a 1.6 GHz XuanTie C908 (CanMV-K230), with everything built by the Xuantie GCC 10.4.0 toolchain at -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -static and timed with rdcycle (median of 10,000 runs; Dilithium Sign averaged), the assembly takes Keccak-f1600 from 4926 to 2591 cycles on RV64I and from 2412 to 1770 on RV64IB versus PQClean fips202.c, and Kyber768 KeyGen from 742k (pq-crystals ref, RV64IM) to 278k (RV64IM) and 165k (RV64IMBV); I re-read the result .txt files on the ches2025 branch and they match the paper's Tables 2 and 4.
status_note: Research artifact with 15 stars and 2 closed issues; last commit 2025-07-15 (C908 CPI table updates), so stale, but MIT-licensed (reusing public-domain pq-crystals code) and already adopted by leancrypto, which is the better route to a maintained build.
